Thanks Elena — and thanks for the clear asks.

Quick answers up front:
- Operator access: we can scope "operator access" to a named operator role limited to witness-only access for snapshot validation (read-only, no key export). We'll provide an operator attestation and time-limited console session narrative in Exhibit A.
- Third-party validator: VeriDoc has a standard engagement model (attestation report + limited on-site/remote verification). I attached their terms and our suggested Exhibit A redlines (v3).

Proposed path:
1) Redwood accepts a third-party attestation (VeriDoc). They will validate a sealed snapshot and issue an attestation memo identifying what was checked.
2) Redwood delivers a sealed snapshot into a short-term, encrypted deposit managed by Veridoc; the snapshot is not functional without keys and the validator only confirms existence and integrity.
3) We include a narrow license exhibit that permits the validator to access the sealed artifact for the purpose of attestation only.

If legal prefers escrow instead, we will need to map a specific custody workflow (who holds keys, recovery triggers). Our preference is the validator route because it retains customer confidentiality while providing the same assurance level.

Paul — if your team can share a short list of minimal redline items for Exhibit A, I can circulate a proposed compromise text to accelerate sign-off.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Strategic Accounts
